full_judgment: 14. Admittedly, as per the CS and SA Khatian, the suit property measuring 88 decimals of land was debutter property as the property of the Bura Kali Deity for the use of the people in general belonging to the Hindu community to perform puja and other religious functions. As per section 20(5) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, even the rent-receiving interest of debutter property is beyond the scope and application of the Act, and the same is retainable by and in favour of the deity. Once the property is debutter property, it cannot vest in the Government. Accordingly, prima facie, the Government having treated it as the khas land of the Government granted settlement of the same in favour of other defendants via different Settlement Cases in 1978-79 and then in 1994-95. Though the property was recorded in the Khas SA Khatian No.1, in the remark column of the said khatian, it was remarked that the same is possessed by the Bura Kali Deity and is used by the local people in general belonging to the Hindu community for performing puja and other religious functions. In such facts and circumstances, the predecessor in the office of the plaintiff filed Miscellaneous Case No.78/ XIII/04-05 for cancellation of the settlement granted via Settlement Miscellaneous Case No.513/XIII/78-79, but without dismissing the said case, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Chapainawabgonj suo-moto granted lease of 10 decimals of land in favour of the deity for the same purpose of performing puja and other religious functions by the people in general of the locality belonging to the Hindu community, and, as such, such a settlement was not called for under any law.
